tfc4e66fcd: Serving data subjects also means knowing what to keep and for how long. tb1be3a3fc: The policy changes, the file gets replaced in the folder and, a year later, nobody can say which wording was in force when that person signed. If something changed between the signature and the dispute, the company has no way to show that the rule it is enforcing is the same one it presented. And a spreadsheet can be edited by anyone with access, without leaving a trace.
tb9a2393e3: One clarification: the hash doesn’t hide anything. The policy text stays readable for everyone; the code simply identifies that exact wording, uniquely. That’s why it can be safely shown on the receipt and in the report, and anyone with the text in hand can check whether they’re looking at the same wording.
tc02053a81: Refusal with justification: anyone who disagrees records the reason, and the company addresses the issue instead of finding out too late.
tc1938f517: The solution starts with treating each policy as a versioned document. When a version is published, the system calculates its SHA-256 hash: a 64-character code that works as the text’s fingerprint. The same wording always produces the same code; any change, however small, produces a completely different one.
tcfe17e144: In Brazil, Provisional Measure (MP) 2,200-2/2001, which created ICP-Brasil (the Brazilian public-key infrastructure), states in art. 10, §2 that it does not prevent the use of other means of proving the authorship and integrity of electronic documents — including without an ICP-Brasil certificate — as long as the parties accept them as valid or they are accepted by the person against whom they are presented. Brazil’s Code of Civil Procedure, in turn, admits all lawful and morally legitimate means of evidence (art. 369).
td5259b52f: Many companies track policy awareness with an “ok” column in a spreadsheet, a sheet signed during onboarding or an email answered with “noted.” They all share the same weakness: they don’t tie the acknowledgment to the text that was accepted.
